Q: Lambda argument that steals unique_ptr used to do the call A:

This is valid in C++17 and later, and UB before C++17.

In C++17 and later, the standard's [expr.call] says:

The postfix-expression is sequenced before each expression in the expression-list and any default argument.

A function call has the form:

postfix-expression ( expression-listopt )

So in the case of p->call([p2 = std::move(p)] { std::cout << "From lambda" << std::endl; }), the evaluation of p->call is sequenced before the lambda expression.

Per [over.ref], when p is of a class type, p->call is interpreted as (p.operator->())->call. So the result of operator-> is also computed before the evaluation of the lambda expression.

Before C++17, the evaluations of the postfix-expression and of the argument are unsequenced, so the two uses of p have undefined behavior.

Q: How can I start learning C as a complete beginner? A:

Buy "The C programming Language" By Brian W. Kernighan and Dennis M. Ritchie. I think there is 2nd edition. Read it 2-3 times. Install compiler, compile and run examples and your experiments. Then ask questions like this.

Q: What is the best practice for prerequisites in a Makefile with multiple levels of includes in source files? A:

I'm not Lilypond expert - my answer is based on understanding of make, and basic information from Lilypod docs.

The problem you describe is similar to problems developer have with compiling code. A single source file creates an object file, but the source file may reference (via #include, or similar) other files. For "C" (and other languages) that are tools to automatically generate the make dependency file. I'm not aware of any specific Lilypod dependecy generation, but you can quickly build you own.

# Makefile

pdf/piano.pdf: parts/piano.ly

depend.mk: parts/piano.ly
    lily-scan.sh pdf/piano.pdf parts/piano.ly > $@

include depend.mk

And you dependency scan is a short shell script: (store in lily-scan.sh, make it executable chmod +x)

#! /bin/sh
# lily-dep.txt TARGET file1.ly file2.ly ...
# Generate make dependencies for TARGET based in \includes in .ly files.
dest=$1
shift
for file ; do
        grep '\\include' $file | sed -E -e 's/.*"([^"]+)"/\1/' -e"s@^@$dest: @" 
done

Few notes:

  1. For a single (or few) files, this is OK.

  2. You can also extend this to support multiple files using make pattern rules.

  3. This simple solution does not handle nested includes.
